import pytest

import jinja2


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_issue_1573_custom_filter_async_true_subscriptable_error():
    jinja_env = jinja2.Environment(enable_async=True)
    jinja_env.filters.update({"add_two": lambda x, y: [i + y for i in x]})

    template = jinja_env.from_string(
        "{% for item in (a.b|add_two(5))[:1] %}{{ item }}{% endfor %}"
    )
    data = {"a": {"b": [1, 2, 3]}}

    # The original bug causes a TypeError: 'coroutine' object is not subscriptable
    # This test should pass once the bug is fixed, producing the expected output.
    result = await template.render_async(data)
    assert result == "6"

    # This part of the test verifies the syntax error described in the report
    # when parentheses are removed. This is not the primary bug, but a related
    # observation.
    with pytest.raises(jinja2.exceptions.TemplateSyntaxError):
        jinja_env.from_string("{% for item in a.b|add_two(5)[:1] %}{{ item }}{% endfor %}")
